class.name: DDGIVolume
class.brief_description: Ray traced dynamic diffuse global illumination (DDGI) for the scene.
class.description: Adds dynamic diffuse global illumination (DDGI) to the scene: grids of irradiance probes that trace rays every frame with hardware ray tracing. Opaque surfaces get their diffuse indirect light from the probes. Lights, emissive materials, the sky and geometry can all change at runtime; the indirect light follows over a few frames. The node drives the [code]ddgi_*[/code] properties of the [Environment] of its [World3D] (the [WorldEnvironment]), and turns DDGI off when it leaves the scene. Use one [DDGIVolume] per scene; with several, the last one that changed wins. By default the probes fill the box given by [member size], centered on the node. With [member follow_camera], they follow the camera instead and the box only sets how many probes there are. The workload (rays per probe, probes updated per frame, probe resolution) is set in [member ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/ddgi/quality]. The probes can be baked (Bake DDGI in the 3D editor toolbar, or [method bake]): with [member bake_mode] set to [constant BAKE_MODE_BAKED_DYNAMIC] the game starts with finished indirect light instead of converging over the first seconds, with [constant BAKE_MODE_BAKED] it traces no rays at all. [b]Note:[/b] Updating the probes needs the Forward+ renderer and the Vulkan rendering driver on a GPU with ray tracing. Elsewhere (D3D12, GPUs without ray tracing) only [constant BAKE_MODE_BAKED] with baked probes works; otherwise DDGI does nothing and the scene renders as without it. Mobile and Compatibility don't support DDGI. [b]Note:[/b] SDFGI and [VoxelGI] are skipped for views that use DDGI, so indirect light isn't counted twice. Objects with a [LightmapGI] lightmap keep it. [b]Note:[/b] The probe grid is always aligned with the world axes; the node's rotation and scale are ignored.

method.name: bake
method.description: Traces the probes until they converge and returns the result, which is also assigned to [member probe_data]. Every probe is updated about [param updates_per_probe] times (with [code]0[/code], 128); the second half of the updates averages over a longer time, so the result is less noisy than the running probes. Blocks until it is done; in the editor a progress dialog shows (and can cancel) it. Returns [code]null[/code] when cancelled or when DDGI can't run. The volume must be fixed ([member follow_camera] off) and in a scene with a [WorldEnvironment], and the renderer must support DDGI updates (Forward+, Vulkan, ray tracing). Save the result with [ResourceSaver] to keep it; the editor's Bake DDGI button does that.

members.member: If [code]true[/code], DDGI darkens its indirect light where nearby geometry blocks it (corners, the floor under objects, around moving objects, also off screen). It needs no rays: the probes' distance maps tell whether points around each surface are free. It is coarse (about the probe spacing) and complements [member Environment.ssao_enabled], which adds the fine contact detail. Direct light and reflections aren't affected. Works with baked probes and without ray tracing hardware. Costs about 0.4 ms at 1920×1080 on an RTX 3060 (a quarter of that with [member ProjectSettings.rendering/global_illumination/gi/use_half_resolution]). Use the Ambient Occlusion [member debug_mode] to tune it.
How far around a surface geometry counts as occluding, in meters. It is limited to the probe spacing of the finest cascade covering the surface: beyond that, the probe grid would show in the result.
How much the ambient occlusion darkens the indirect light: [code]0.0[/code] none, [code]1.0[/code] fully.

How the probes use [member probe_data]. See [enum BakeMode]. When the baked data doesn't fit the volume (it was moved, resized, or its probe spacing or cascades changed), the probes are updated dynamically until baked again, and a configuration warning says so.

Multiplier for the light passed on from one bounce to the next inside the probes. Above [code]1.0[/code], rooms lit indirectly (interiors behind a window, corridors) get brighter, more than surfaces lit directly; the result is averaged over time like all probe light, so it doesn't flicker. [code]1.0[/code] is physically based; at most [code]2.0[/code]. Unlike [member energy], it changes the light the probes see, so baked probes must be baked again.
The number of probe grids. Each cascade has twice the probe spacing of the previous one and covers twice the distance, so far surfaces get coarser indirect light.
Shows the indirect light, the probes or the cascades instead of the normal image, for finding lighting problems. See [enum Environment.DDGIDebugMode].
If [code]true[/code], DDGI is on. If [code]false[/code], the scene renders without it.

If [code]true[/code], the probe grids follow the camera and scroll as it moves, so DDGI covers any area. [member size] and [member probe_spacing] then only set the number of probes per axis. If [code]false[/code], the probes stay in the box around the node.

How much of a probe's previous light is kept at each update. Higher values give less noise but slower reaction to light changes. A light change that two updates in a row agree on lowers it for a while; ray noise doesn't. Probe directions whose light comes from a few bright rays (a window, a small lamp) keep more of their previous light.
Offset of the probe lookup along the surface normal, as a fraction of the probe spacing. Raise it against dark blotches near corners (self shadowing).
If [code]true[/code], probes inside geometry are switched off and probes with no surface nearby are updated less often. Saves ray tracing time.
The baked probes, made by [method bake]. Used according to [member bake_mode].
If [code]true[/code], probes that end up inside or too close to geometry are moved away from it (by at most half a cell), which reduces light leaks and dark spots.
The distance between probes of the finest cascade, in meters. Smaller spacing gives more detailed indirect light and fewer leaks through thin walls, but needs more probes for the same area.

The size of the box filled with probes, in meters. The number of probes per axis is [code]size / probe_spacing + 1[/code] (at most 64 per axis). The box can be resized with the gizmo handles in the 3D editor.
Offset of the probe lookup toward the camera, as a fraction of the probe spacing. Raise it against dark blotches and leaks.

constants.constant: The probes are traced at runtime; [member probe_data] isn't used.

The probes are taken from [member probe_data] and never updated: no rays are traced, so the indirect light doesn't react to changes, but it costs only the lookup and also works without ray tracing hardware (D3D12 driver, older GPUs).

The probes start from [member probe_data] and are then updated at runtime like [constant BAKE_MODE_DYNAMIC]: the indirect light is right from the first frame and still follows lights and objects that change.
